title: How Student Drivers Should Handle Aggressive Drivers
hook: Terrified of crazy drivers honking while you're learning?

script.narration: Terrified of crazy drivers tailgating or honking while you're learning to drive? Here is the golden defensive driving rule you need.
script.visual_search: tailgating car viewed from rear window mirror

script.narration: When an aggressive driver tailgates you, never speed up past your comfort level or stomp your brakes out of anger.
Instead, gently increase the space in FRONT of your car. Doubling your safe following distance gives you buffer space to stop slowly if needed.
script.visual_search: car driving safely on open road distance

script.narration: Never make eye contact or engage. Maintain your lane, stay calm, and allow them to pass safely at the next safe opportunity.
script.visual_search: car passing another vehicle on multi lane highway

script.narration: Stay calm and safe on the road. Subscribe for essential safety tips every student driver needs!
script.visual_search: confident young driver smiling in car

description:
Learning to drive alongside aggressive drivers can be terrifying for students. This short guide breaks down defensive driving techniques to keep you calm and safe under pressure.

Discover why increasing your forward distance protects you from tailgaters and how to manage road stress during your student driving practice sessions.

Subscribe to the channel for practical educational shorts on road safety and driving tips.
why_it_will_work: Reflects the emotional trigger of the viral 'crazy driver/student driver' trend while offering valuable educational defensive driving tactics that promote viewer retention.
fact_check_notes: Confirm defensive driving best practices regarding safe following distances (e.g., 3-to-4 second rule).
